paragraphs: An image signal processor turns raw camera measurements into an image. Its processing choices affect both visual quality and how well an object detector works. AdaptiveISP addresses a mismatch in existing approaches: optimizing images to look good does not necessarily produce the best inputs for detection, and a fixed processing pipeline can struggle as scenes change.

The method learns to choose both the processing modules and their parameters for each input. It uses deep reinforcement learning with detection performance as the objective. Its design follows the observation that most images need only a few processing steps, while a smaller number benefit from more extensive processing.

The reported experiments show better object detection than prior state-of-the-art approaches, together with dynamic control over the balance between detection performance and computation. This makes the contribution more than another parameter-tuning method: it adapts the amount and structure of image processing to the scene. The abstract particularly highlights scenes with large variations in dynamic range.
neurips-2024-adaptiveisp-learning-an-ada.tldr: AdaptiveISP learns scene-dependent image-processing pipelines that improve object detection while adjusting computational cost.

paragraphs: Long-context language models store keys and values from earlier tokens so that later generation can attend to them. This cache consumes memory and makes attention more expensive as context grows. Removing less useful tokens helps, but ArkVale starts from an important observation: a token that appears unimportant now may become useful again during later decoding steps.

ArkVale manages the cache in pages and makes eviction reversible. It asynchronously backs up completed pages in external memory, such as CPU memory, and creates a compact summary of each page using a bounding volume of its keys. Before attention, these summaries help rank pages, bring important ones back, and remove less important ones.

Attention then uses only selected pages. Experiments report negligible accuracy loss on various long-context tasks with cache budgets of 2k–4k, alongside decoding speedups of 2.2 times and batching throughput improvements of 4.6 times. The central contribution is a cache policy that responds to changing relevance while reducing active memory use and attention work.
neurips-2024-arkvale-efficient-generativ.tldr: ArkVale reduces long-context inference costs by evicting cache pages while retaining the ability to recall them when their tokens become relevant again.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning systems often improve their use of training experience through changes to the learning algorithm. This paper investigates another route: increasing model capacity. It studies how larger networks interact with techniques designed specifically for reinforcement learning, using the empirical findings to develop BRO, short for Bigger, Regularized, Optimistic.

The central design choice is to scale the critic networks, which provide evaluations used in learning, while applying strong regularization. The authors find that regularization enables this increase in capacity to work effectively. BRO combines these larger critics with optimistic exploration, bringing together model scale, constraints on learning, and an exploration strategy.

Across 40 tasks from DeepMind Control, MetaWorld, and MyoSuite, BRO reportedly outperforms leading model-based and model-free algorithms. The authors also report the first model-free achievement of near-optimal policies on the challenging Dog and Humanoid tasks. These findings support scaling as a useful source of sample-efficiency improvements when paired with the right reinforcement-learning design choices.
neurips-2024-bigger-regularized-optimist.tldr: BRO combines larger, strongly regularized critics with optimistic exploration to improve continuous-control reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: Explaining how a prediction depends on an input can require more than changing that input in isolation. If one variable causally affects others, changing it may also change several inputs to the model. Causal Dependence Plots visualize how predictions respond when these downstream changes are included in the explanation.

The framework extends Partial Dependence Plots, retaining them as a special case while supporting other causal interpretations. In particular, it can represent total, direct, and indirect effects. These views separate different ways that a change can influence a prediction, giving the reader more specific explanations than a single association between an input and output.

Through simulations and experiments with real data, the authors demonstrate that the plots can be combined with causal-learning methods and sensitivity analysis. Their contribution is a modular way to connect model interpretation with causal reasoning. The proposed uses include scientific machine learning and algorithmic fairness, where the consequences of changing an input can matter as much as its predictive association.
neurips-2024-causal-dependence-plots-c1f.tldr: Causal Dependence Plots explain predictions by accounting for both changes to an input and the resulting causal changes to other inputs.

paragraphs: Compositional generalization means applying learned components in new combinations. Neural networks still struggle with this, especially without extensive pretraining. Hybrid systems that combine neural learning and symbolic computation can help, but the paper argues that making neural networks merely configure a symbolic system limits scalability and flexibility.

The authors instead develop a unified approach in which the same transformations have both neural and symbolic interpretations. They extend the Differentiable Tree Machine in two ways. Sparse vector representations make symbolic structures more efficient to handle, and changes to the architecture expand its scope from transforming trees into trees to transforming sequences into sequences.

The improved model reportedly preserves its previous generalization capabilities while becoming substantially more efficient and more broadly applicable. A fully neural path through the network is central to the design: symbolic structure remains interpretable without requiring all computation to pass through a separate symbolic mechanism. The result advances a particular architecture for combining structured reasoning with neural computation.
neurips-2024-compositional-generalizatio.tldr: Sparse representations and sequence processing make the Differentiable Tree Machine more efficient and broadly applicable while preserving its generalization capabilities.

paragraphs: Sequential recommendation predicts a user's next interaction from their previous interactions. One approach turns these histories into instructions and adapts a language model using LoRA, a method that trains a limited set of additional parameters. The paper identifies a problem with sharing the same adaptation across very different histories: learning from one sequence can interfere with learning from another.

Instance-wise LoRA, or iLoRA, treats recommendation as a multi-task problem and combines LoRA with a mixture of experts. Different experts are encouraged to represent different aspects of user behavior. A gate uses a representation of each interaction sequence to decide how strongly each expert participates, making the adaptation depend on the particular sequence.

Experiments on three benchmark datasets support improved recommendation accuracy and reduced negative transfer. Compared with basic LoRA, iLoRA reports an average relative improvement of 11.4% in hit ratio with less than a 1% relative increase in trainable parameters. The result shows that customizing how adaptation parameters are used can provide gains without substantially expanding their number.
neurips-2024-customizing-language-models.tldr: iLoRA combines adaptation experts differently for each user sequence to improve recommendations with little additional parameter cost.

paragraphs: Molecular docking predicts how a ligand fits into a protein, helping researchers study interactions relevant to drug design. Geometric deep learning has improved docking speed and accuracy, but existing approaches can be specialized to particular settings. The paper also highlights difficulties involving protein side chains, large binding pockets, and structures that are not physically valid.

DeltaDock organizes docking into two stages: identifying a binding pocket and placing the ligand within it. For the first stage, it frames pocket prediction as aligning a pocket with the ligand. The second stage uses a two-level, coarse-to-fine refinement process that repeatedly improves the proposed docking arrangement.

The experiments report strong performance across docking settings. In blind docking, DeltaDock improves the success rate by 31% relative to DiffDock, the prior leading geometric deep learning model identified in the abstract. When physical validity is included in evaluation, the reported relative improvement rises to about 300%. This distinction emphasizes that predicting a successful pose and producing a physically acceptable structure are both important outcomes.
neurips-2024-deltadock-a-unified-framewo.tldr: DeltaDock combines pocket–ligand alignment with iterative pose refinement to improve docking accuracy and physical validity.

paragraphs: Planning how to synthesize a molecule often involves working backward from the desired product to available building blocks. Many search methods consider any suitable building blocks an acceptable endpoint. This paper addresses a more constrained task: finding a synthesis route that uses particular starting materials desired by the user.

Double-Ended Synthesis Planning, or DESP, searches from both ends. It interleaves expansions from the target molecule with expansions from the specified starting materials, making the starting-material requirement part of the search. A goal-conditioned cost network guides the process. That network is trained offline using a partially observed hypergraph of valid chemical reactions.

On multiple new benchmarks, DESP improves solve rates and reduces the number of search expansions by directing planning toward expert goals. It can also use existing models for individual retrosynthesis steps. The authors anticipate further improvements as those models improve, but that scaling expectation is prospective. The demonstrated contribution is a search formulation and algorithm that explicitly accommodate required starting materials.
neurips-2024-double-ended-synthesis-plan.tldr: DESP searches from both a target molecule and required starting materials to find constrained synthesis routes more effectively.

paragraphs: Evaluating a policy from historical transitions becomes harder when the future environment may differ from the observed one. This paper estimates best- and worst-case policy values under specified changes to an environment. The data may come from the policy being evaluated or from a different policy.

The proposed model bounds changes to transition densities by a chosen multiplicative factor and its reciprocal. Within this model, the authors characterize sharp value bounds: the tightest bounds supported by the original transition observations. They then develop an estimator that is semiparametrically efficient and remains so when certain auxiliary functions are learned at slow, nonparametric rates.

The estimator is also asymptotically normal, supporting Wald confidence intervals. If certain auxiliary estimates are inconsistent, the method can still yield valid bounds, although those bounds may no longer be sharp. Numerical simulations validate the stated properties. The contribution combines a defined model of environmental change with statistical procedures that account for estimation uncertainty and selected kinds of auxiliary-model error.
neurips-2024-efficient-and-sharp-off-pol.tldr: The paper develops statistically efficient estimates of tight policy-value bounds under a specified model of environmental change.

paragraphs: Federated learning lets clients train a shared model without directly sharing their sensitive data. Understanding what each client contributes remains difficult, particularly as behavior changes during training. Federated Behavioural Planes address this interpretability problem by tracking clients through two different views of their behavior.

One view focuses on predictive errors, while the other focuses on decision-making through counterfactual behavior. Together, these views produce trajectories describing how clients evolve and contribute to the global model. The experiments show that these trajectories are informative and reveal groups of clients that behave similarly.

The authors also use the discovered patterns to build Federated Behavioural Shields, a robust aggregation technique that detects malicious or noisy client models. It reportedly surpasses existing state-of-the-art federated-learning defenses in the experiments. The paper therefore connects explanation with intervention: representations developed to make client behavior understandable also provide signals for protecting the shared training process. Its findings concern both visibility into training dynamics and improved handling of problematic contributions.
neurips-2024-federated-behavioural-plane.tldr: Federated Behavioural Planes track client behavior over training and support an aggregation defense against malicious or noisy contributions.

paragraphs: Federated learning allows institutions to collaborate without pooling their original datasets, but information exchanged during training can still expose private data. The paper points to reconstruction risks involving transferred gradients or knowledge of client model architectures. It addresses these concerns for semantic segmentation, where models assign categories to image regions at the pixel level.

BlackFed adapts client networks without exchanging gradients or model architecture information between clients and the server. It uses zero-order optimization to update client weights and first-order optimization to update server weights. This combination lets the client side operate as a black box while maintaining a federated learning process.

The authors evaluate the framework on several computer vision and medical imaging datasets and report that it is effective. They describe it as one of the first federated segmentation approaches to avoid both gradient and model-information exchange. Its privacy contribution is the removal of those information-sharing pathways; the abstract presents this as better privacy preservation, without claiming an unconditional guarantee against every form of data disclosure.
neurips-2024-federated-black-box-adaptat.tldr: BlackFed enables federated semantic segmentation without exchanging client gradients or model architecture information.

paragraphs: This paper examines whether language has statistical structure that repeats across different scales. It reports self-similarity, with complexity appearing at multiple levels rather than one characteristic context length. It also finds long-range dependence, quantified by a Hurst parameter of approximately 0.7.

The authors use these findings to argue that dependencies within shorter passages can resemble dependencies across larger spans of text. This offers a possible explanation for why predicting the next token can help a model capture broader textual structure and intent. The proposed connection is explanatory rather than a demonstration that fractal structure alone causes the success of language models.

Analyses across domains and model architectures find that the fractal parameters are robust. Small differences in these parameters across language models also predict downstream performance better than the perplexity-based bits-per-byte measure in the reported analysis. The work thus contributes both a quantitative description of language structure and an empirical signal for assessing models, while presenting the link to next-token prediction as a promising interpretation.
neurips-2024-fractal-patterns-may-illumi.tldr: Measured self-similarity and long-range dependence in language offer a possible explanation for next-token prediction's broader effectiveness.

paragraphs: A memorization network fits every example in a finite dataset, but fitting those examples does not by itself establish performance on new data. This paper theoretically studies that distinction for independently and identically distributed training samples, under mild conditions on the data distribution.

The authors construct memorization networks with minimal parameter counts, including constructions with a constant number of parameters. They then show that generalizable memorization networks must have width at least equal to the data dimension in their setting. This requirement implies that existing constructions optimized for parameter count are not generalizable under the analysis.

The paper also derives sample-complexity bounds, including an exact result for memorization algorithms with constant parameter counts. It establishes that some distributions require exponentially many parameters in the data dimension for generalizable memorization. Finally, it gives an efficient, generalizable algorithm when the sample count exceeds the distribution's efficient memorization sample complexity. Together, these results separate compact representation of training data from the resources needed to generalize.
neurips-2024-generalizablity-of-memoriza.tldr: The paper characterizes when memorization networks can generalize, identifying width, sample, and distribution-dependent parameter requirements.

paragraphs: The Bahncard problem concerns repeated decisions between a cheaper short-term option and a more expensive long-term option when future demand is unknown. Each decision is irreversible, so a choice that looks economical now may turn out poorly as later needs become clear. It generalizes the classic ski-rental problem.

The paper introduces PFSUM, an algorithm that combines historical information with predictions about the near future. This makes it a learning-augmented online algorithm: decisions still arrive over time, but forecasts supplement what has already been observed. The approach gives both past activity and anticipated short-term activity a role in deciding when the long-term option is worthwhile.

The authors derive a competitive ratio that depends on prediction error, explicitly connecting the performance guarantee to forecast quality. Extensive experiments also show PFSUM outperforming the previously developed primal-dual learning-augmented algorithm. The theoretical and empirical contributions address complementary questions: how the algorithm's guarantee changes with imperfect predictions, and how it compares with the existing approach in the evaluated cases.
neurips-2024-learning-augmented-algorith.tldr: PFSUM combines past observations with short-term forecasts to improve online Bahncard decisions, with guarantees tied to prediction error.

paragraphs: Objects in a video can be separated by observing which points move together. Earlier motion-based segmentation methods often use optical flow, which captures motion over a short interval. This paper trains a segmentation network with longer point trajectories as an additional supervisory signal, using motion without other forms of supervision.

Long trajectories provide information across time, but their complex motion is difficult to capture with a fixed parametric model. The authors instead borrow an idea from subspace clustering. Their loss encourages groups of trajectories to form low-rank matrices, so that the movement of a point can be approximately represented by a linear combination of other tracks in its group.

This formulation turns relationships among trajectories into a training signal without requiring a detailed model of every possible motion pattern. The method outperforms previous approaches on motion-based segmentation in the reported results. That finding supports both the usefulness of longer-term motion information and the proposed way of organizing it, with optical flow and extended tracks contributing complementary supervision.
neurips-2024-learning-segmentation-from-.tldr: Grouping long-term point trajectories through a low-rank training objective improves motion-based video segmentation.

paragraphs: The sparse parity problem is a theoretical benchmark in which the answer depends on the parity of a selected subset of input coordinates. This paper studies whether gradient-based training of a neural network can solve it with complexity comparable to established statistical-query bounds.

The method uses sign stochastic gradient descent on a two-layer fully connected network. For inputs on a d-dimensional hypercube and k at most on the order of the square root of d, the authors report sample complexity of approximately d to the power k minus one, suppressing logarithmic factors, with a neuron count exponential in k.

The proof first constructs a network that solves the parity problem correctly, then shows that sign-based training can approximate this network with small statistical errors. The authors characterize the result as matching the established statistical-query lower bound and, to their knowledge, the first gradient-based result to do so. The contribution is a theoretical training guarantee under the stated sparsity and network-size conditions.
neurips-2024-matching-the-statistical-qu.tldr: The paper proves that sign-based stochastic gradient training can solve sparse parity with complexity characterized as matching statistical-query lower bounds.

paragraphs: Running language models on CPUs is challenging partly because attention requires many multiply-add operations. NoMAD-Attention changes how attention scores are computed to exploit a specific CPU capability: SIMD registers can perform batches of lookups with very low latency.

The algorithm replaces multiply-add work in its attention computation with repeated lookups inside these registers. Its design therefore connects the attention algorithm directly to the hardware operations that CPUs can execute quickly. It can be applied to pretrained attention-based language models without fine-tuning, allowing the computational change to be used with an existing model.

The empirical evaluation reports that model quality is well maintained. For a 4-bit quantized model based on LLaMA-7B at a context length of 16k, the reported speedup reaches up to two times. This is a result for the evaluated configuration, rather than a uniform speedup claim for every model or context length. The paper's central contribution is a hardware-aware route to faster CPU attention through register-based lookup operations.
neurips-2024-nomad-attention-efficient-l.tldr: NoMAD-Attention replaces attention multiply-add operations with fast CPU register lookups, speeding inference without model fine-tuning.

paragraphs: Spectral bisection divides a graph into two equally sized communities using an eigenvector of its Laplacian. It has recovery guarantees for certain random graph models, but those guarantees can be sensitive to how accurately the model describes the graph. This paper investigates robustness when an adversary changes the model in ways consistent with the true communities.

The allowed changes include adding edges within communities or increasing their probability. Although these changes seem helpful, they test whether an algorithm depends too strongly on precise statistical assumptions. The authors identify a broad range of such adversaries for which spectral bisection with the unnormalized Laplacian exactly recovers the planted partition.

For many of the same settings, normalized spectral bisection instead misclassifies a constant fraction of vertices. Numerical experiments complement the theoretical results. The contrast shows that the choice of Laplacian can fundamentally affect robustness, even when modifications reinforce within-community connections. The positive result applies to the identified adversary settings rather than to all possible departures from the random graph model.
neurips-2024-on-the-robustness-of-spectr.tldr: Under many semirandom graph changes, unnormalized spectral bisection recovers communities exactly while its normalized counterpart makes substantial errors.

paragraphs: Privacy requirements can make learning statistically difficult, motivating the use of public data alongside private samples. In the setting studied here, privacy must always hold for the private samples. Learning guarantees additionally depend on the private and public data distributions being sufficiently close.

Earlier work showed that enough unlabeled public data could make private learning statistically feasible, but the resulting algorithms were computationally inefficient. This paper provides algorithms that provably use public data for private learning whenever the function class is learnable without privacy. Their efficiency is measured by the number of calls to an optimization oracle for that class.

That qualification defines the computational contribution: the result bounds reliance on an optimization capability, rather than independently establishing the cost of implementing that capability for every class. The authors also give specialized algorithms with improved sample complexity for convex function classes and binary classification. Together, these results connect public-data assistance with computationally efficient private learning under the stated distributional and oracle framework.
neurips-2024-oracle-efficient-differenti.tldr: The paper gives oracle-efficient private-learning algorithms that use public data, with learning guarantees when public and private distributions are sufficiently close.

paragraphs: Language models are often ranked by asking which of two answers people prefer. Because human comparisons are expensive, practitioners also use a strong language model as a judge. This introduces a statistical problem: the judge's preferences may differ from human preferences, affecting both rankings and confidence in them.

The paper combines a small collection of human comparisons with a large collection of model-generated comparisons. Instead of assigning each model only one rank, the framework produces a set of possible ranking positions. It gives an asymptotic coverage guarantee at a user-selected probability level for the true ranking defined by the distribution of human preferences.

Experiments use human judgments from LMSYS Chatbot Arena and comparisons from three strong language models. They demonstrate the framework's effectiveness and show that rank sets based only on model judges often disagree with human preferences. The contribution is a way to use abundant automated judgments while explicitly accounting for uncertainty arising from their mismatch with the human target.
neurips-2024-prediction-powered-ranking-.tldr: The framework combines human and automated comparisons to produce language-model rank sets with asymptotic coverage guarantees.

paragraphs: A single image does not directly reveal absolute scene scale because perspective projection loses that information. Many depth models therefore predict relative depth rather than distances in metric units. RSA investigates whether a description of the objects in an image can help align those relative predictions with metric depth.

The method uses a text caption to predict the parameters of a linear transformation applied across the entire relative depth map. Its motivation is that objects are associated with particular scene types: the objects named in a caption can provide contextual information relevant to scale. RSA supplies an alignment module for an existing depth prediction.

The authors demonstrate the approach with general-purpose depth models on indoor NYUv2 and VOID data and outdoor KITTI data. With training across multiple datasets, it can also act as a zero-shot alignment module. Reported predictions improve on common alignment practices and approach the reference obtained by fitting relative depth directly to ground truth with a linear transformation.
neurips-2024-rsa-resolving-scale-ambigui.tldr: RSA uses image captions to predict a global linear transformation that converts relative depth estimates into metric-scaled predictions.

paragraphs: Human-oriented binary reverse engineering tries to turn compiled code into descriptions that people can understand, such as summaries and function names. The challenge is to connect binary representations with the meanings expressed in source code. This paper combines models trained on the two forms of code to help bridge that gap.

Its probe-and-recover framework uses a binary–source encoder–decoder model together with black-box language models. Knowledge from pretrained source-code models is used to generate relevant code fragments containing informative symbols. These fragments become additional context for the black-box model when it recovers human-readable information from a binary.

The reported zero-shot summarization gains are 10.3% relative on CHRF and 16.7% relative on a GPT4-based metric. For function-name recovery, token-level precision and recall rise by 6.7 and 7.4 percentage points, respectively. These results support the idea that source-code knowledge can improve binary analysis through synthesized context, allowing complementary code models to contribute to the recovery task.
neurips-2024-source-code-foundation-mode.tldr: A probe-and-recover framework turns source-code model knowledge into context that improves binary summaries and function-name recovery.

paragraphs: Symmetry discovery seeks transformations that preserve meaningful structure in data. Such knowledge can improve machine-learning tasks, but the paper notes that existing continuous-symmetry experiments have largely focused on affine transformations. The authors develop a framework intended to reach beyond that transformation family.

The framework assumes the data have an underlying manifold structure. Under this assumption, it supports discovery of continuous symmetries beyond the affine group. The paper also supplies a related framework for discrete symmetries, extending the scope of the proposed approach to another kind of structure-preserving transformation.

Experiments compare the method with LieGAN. For affine symmetry detection, the proposed method is competitive when many samples are available and performs better with small sample sizes. It also detects continuous symmetries outside the affine group and is generally more computationally efficient than LieGAN. The findings therefore address both breadth and practicality: the framework captures a broader class of transformations while showing favorable sample-size and computational behavior in the reported comparisons.
neurips-2024-symmetry-discovery-beyond-a.tldr: Under a manifold assumption, the proposed framework discovers continuous symmetries beyond affine transformations and compares favorably with LieGAN.

paragraphs: Recognizing harmful visual content requires attention to context, not just the presence of a small set of objects. This paper introduces VHD11K to broaden the content covered by harmfulness datasets. It contains 10,000 images and 1,000 videos across 10 harmful categories, combining Internet material with outputs from four generative models.

The authors also propose an annotation process framed as visual question answering. Three vision-language models debate whether an image or video is harmful, with in-context learning incorporated into that process. The aim is to consider contextual evidence and competing interpretations before assigning a label, reducing misjudgments in ambiguous cases.

The evaluation reports strong agreement between this annotation framework and human judgments. The dataset also exposes gaps in existing harmful-content detectors and improves recognition methods, with larger improvements than the SMID baseline dataset. These findings support both the annotation approach and the value of broader training and evaluation coverage, including generated content and harmful concepts that require contextual interpretation.
neurips-2024-t2vs-meet-vlms-a-scalable-m.tldr: VHD11K combines diverse real and generated visual content with multi-model contextual annotation to improve harmfulness recognition.

paragraphs: Discovering formulas for mathematical constants is difficult because a numerically close expression need not reveal a correct identity. The paper addresses this lack of a useful distance measure by comparing how formulas converge, rather than comparing only the numerical values they approach.

These convergence-based metrics support categorization, characterization, and automated clustering of formulas. The authors apply the method to polynomial continued fractions, a family connected to mathematical constants and many mathematical structures. Grouping formulas by their convergence behavior provides a way to search for patterns without relying on near-equality of their final values.

The study examines 1,768,900 formulas, identifying known expressions and discovering previously unknown formulas for pi, the natural logarithm of two, Gauss' constant, and the lemniscate constant. Patterns found through the method also allow individual formulas to be generalized into infinite families. The authors present this as a step toward generative systems that produce formulas with specified mathematical properties; that generative capability is a future direction rather than the demonstrated system itself.
neurips-2024-unsupervised-discovery-of-f.tldr: Clustering formulas by their convergence dynamics reveals new expressions for mathematical constants and patterns extending to infinite families.
